display_title: Anthropic Pledges Equity to Public Benefit Fund
display_title_he: אנתרופיק תקצה מניות לקרן לתועלת הציבור
short_summary: Anthropic has committed five percent of its equity to a public benefit fund ahead of its public offering. The initiative aims to address technological labor disruption while barring political lobbying.

sources.name: Walla
sources.title: צעד חסר תקדים: מפתחת קלוד תקצה 5% מהמניות "לתועלת הציבור"

paragraphs: Artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic, widely recognized as the developer of the Claude chatbot, has announced a landmark commitment to allocate five percent of its equity to a newly established public benefit fund. According to statements released by the company, this structural mechanism will provide significantly enhanced flexibility and expanded operational scale, allowing leadership to direct meaningful philanthropic contributions toward what it characterizes as the public good.

The proposed vehicle will be organized under the legal structure of a wholly owned limited liability company. Beyond this initial allocation of equity, the fund will be formally eligible to receive an additional two percent of Anthropic shares—granted at the sole discretion of the board of directors—for every fifty percent increase in company valuation above a baseline threshold that remains undisclosed to the public. This significant financial arrangement coincides with preparations for what is projected to be one of the largest initial public offerings in history staged as a public benefit corporation. Under this designated legal format, corporate directors and executives are bound by charter obligations to balance broad societal considerations against the conventional fiduciary responsibility of maximizing shareholder financial returns.

Consistently marketing itself as an artificial intelligence laboratory that places safety at the forefront of its operational agenda, Anthropic has previously warned that artificial intelligence could potentially introduce catastrophic or existential risks to humanity. Highlighting this risk-averse stance, the company dedicated approximately eighty pages out of the 261 pages in its primary prospectus report solely to outlining comprehensive risk factors. In an accompanying blog post, the developer explained that the public benefit fund could finance diverse initiatives, including direct grants to non-profit organizations, targeted economic disbursements to specific population groups, and strategic efforts aimed at navigating the profound consequences of rapid technological change on the wider labor market.

Addressing workforce disruptions represents one of the primary areas of concentration for the new fund, building directly upon an earlier commitment of two hundred million dollars that Anthropic pledged to research and mitigate labor instability. Anxiety surrounding the future of work has mounted as several commercial enterprises, especially in the technology sector, have eliminated thousands of jobs following massive investments in artificial intelligence, justifying these cuts through claims of greater productivity and organizational efficiency. These real-world developments reflect warnings highlighted in research published by the International Monetary Fund. That study indicated that approximately forty percent of employment worldwide will experience upgrading, downgrading, or outright elimination due to artificial intelligence, with the organization’s managing director highlighting that this proportion reaches up to sixty percent within advanced industrial economies.

The initiative did not escape public scrutiny from prominent industry rivals. Elon Musk, who leads the competing enterprise xAI, reacted publicly on the social network platform X, commenting that Anthropic ought to deliver the equity directly to the public instead. In response to broader political sensitivities, Anthropic stressed that none of the capital controlled by the philanthropic vehicle will ever be allocated toward lobbying activities or political contributions, whether domestically inside the United States or on foreign soil. This strict governance boundary comes as regulatory authorities and legislators seek to tighten compliance rules surrounding artificial intelligence systems, even as competing technology firms attempt to shape legislative outcomes.

facts.fact: Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI chatbot, announced it will allocate 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund.

The fund will be structured as a wholly owned limited liability company and could receive an additional 2% of shares per 50% valuation increase above an undisclosed baseline, subject to board discretion.
Anthropic is preparing for an initial public offering under the public benefit corporation model, which legally requires considering broader interests alongside shareholder returns.
Anthropic positioned itself as a safety-first AI lab, noting AI could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, and dedicated around 80 of 261 pages in its main prospectus to risk factors.

The fund may support non-profit donations, direct distributions to certain populations, and initiatives targeting AI's impact on employment, following an earlier $200 million pledge for labor disruption research.
An IMF study noted by its managing director indicates roughly 40% of jobs globally—and up to 60% in advanced economies—will be upgraded, downgraded, or eliminated due to AI.
Elon Musk, head of competing firm xAI, criticized the move on X, suggesting the shares should be given directly to the public.
Anthropic stated that none of the fund's capital will be used for lobbying or political contributions in the United States or elsewhere.
